verified_with.checked_via: npm view opencode-ai version; npm install opencode-ai@1.19.5; opencode --version

notes: The scaffold writes one generated plugin file, .opencode/plugins/scaffold-hooks.ts (global scope: ~/.config/opencode/plugins/scaffold-hooks.ts). OpenCode loads direct .ts and .js files from every plugins/ directory without a config entry (docs, Discover section).

OpenCode 1.19.5 runs the V1 API: it called the default export's server() (verified by loading a probe plugin with the real CLI) and did not call setup(). The docs describe a V2 API (Plugin.define with setup(ctx)); the generated plugin exports both from one object, as the docs' 'Support V1' section describes. The V2 half is written to the documented signatures and checked with a fake context only, not against a V2 runtime.
V1 blocks a tool by throwing from tool.execute.before. V2 uses the same throw in ctx.tool.hook('execute.before').

Neither API has a stop or turn-end hook that can block. session.idle is an event; the plugin turns a failing check into a follow-up prompt on the same session (session.promptAsync in V1, ctx.session.prompt in V2) and skips the next idle of that session, which is the stop_hook_active guard.
Subagent sessions have a parentID; the plugin looks the session up (session.get) and ignores sessions that have one. This replaces Froggy's isMainSession condition.

opencode-froggy 1.7.0 (2026-11-01) and later no longer load .opencode/hook/hooks.md, and the config key `plugin` is deprecated in favour of `plugins`; the native plugin needs neither. A refresh removes the managed Froggy block and the plugin entry an earlier scaffold added.

events.name: session.created
events.description: A session was created. Only main sessions run it. Output is not injected into the model context; failures are logged.

events.name: session.idle
events.description: A main session finished its turn. A failing check sends its output back as a prompt once, then the next idle is skipped. Gated by run_on_code_changes.
events.can_block: continues the session instead of blocking

events.name: tool.execute.before
events.description: Before a tool runs. matcher is a regex over the tool name (bash, edit, write, read, ...). A failing check throws and blocks the tool.

events.name: tool.execute.after
events.description: After a tool ran. matcher as above. A failing check is logged; it cannot undo the tool.

not_supported: session.deleted, session.error, message and file events
script_stdin: One JSON object: hook_event_name, session_id, cwd, plus tool_name and tool_input for tool events and stop_hook_active for session.idle.
